text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

COFFEE - Robusta futures in London stepped back from their peaks after earlier trade and speculative buying encountered origin sales but prices still closed firmer. May added $27 to close at $1,641 per tonne, while July closed $38 higher at $1,660 per tonne.

Threats of a strike by stevedores at Brazil's key port of Santos, which is set to spread to a national level on April 4, had little impact on prices. However, with the current low stocks in consumer hands any strike is very sensitive for the market.

Santos is Brazil's largest coffee exporting port accounting for 984,698 60-kg bags of the 1.28 mn bags loaded for March by March 31. A further 238,647 bags has been loaded at Vitoria, 51,865 bags at Rio de Janeiro and 1,245 bags at Varginha. Overall March shipments are expected to finish at between 1.35 to 1.40 mn bags.

Also in New York the threat of a strike in Brazil had little impact on prices as there is general agreement that exports should not be greatly affected. May gave up 1.15 cents/lb to close at 193.15 cents/lb, while July closed 0.90 cents/lb lower at 175.25 cents/lb. The outer months closed 2.55 cents/lb lower to 2.70 cents/lb higher. Traders believe that higher shipments through the middle of the month could keep the market in check. ICO data support the view of high shipments now and reduced supplies later in the season.

ICO - Coffee exports by exporting members of the International Coffee Organization rose to 7.410 mn 60-kg bags in February 1997 from 6.656 mn bags the same month the previous year, the International Coffee Organization said. That brought total exports in October/February 1996/97 up to 34.265 mn bags, up 13 per cent from the 30.300 mn bags shipped the same period in 1995/96. Brazil's market share in October/February 1996/97 rose dramatically to 24.75 per cent from 16.01 per cent the same period in 1995/96 while Colombia's market share declined from 16.28 to 15.26 per cent.

BRAZIL - Brazil's government sold a total of 128,660 60- kg bags or 39.44 per cent of the 326,188 bags offered in its monthly auction on April 2, official sources said. The total revenue from the auction was 16.05 mn reais ($17 mn).

HONG KONG - Hong Kong imported 174,200 bags of coffee in 1996, 11 per cent more than was imported the previous year but 27 per cent less than was imported in 1994. Hong Kong imports most of its coffee in the form of solubles. Main soluble suppliers in 1996 were China (21,600 vs 41,600 bags) and South Korea (22,700 vs 19,200 bags). The country exported 128,000 bags of coffee in 1996, 6 per cent more than was exported the previous year.
